title: Shapes of the guarantees of the verified Balancer V2 repair

definitions.guarantee: One locked requirement theorem of the task (task.json, spec/<lib>/Challenge.lean). Its statement in plain language is the doc comment of the property it asserts in the locked specification, quoted with line breaks joined by spaces; `readme` is the row of the task README's requirement table that names it, when there is one.
definitions.shape: The set of declarations the guarantee uses, directly or through others, following the constants the Lean kernel records in each declaration's type and value (the rule of the home page graph, under `rule`). The guarantee itself is not counted.
definitions.size: The number of declarations in the shape.
definitions.depth: The longest chain of uses from the guarantee down to a declaration that uses no other node: 0 for a declaration that uses none, else one more than its deepest dependency.
definitions.width: width[d] is the number of declarations of the shape whose own depth is d, for d from 0 to depth - 1.
definitions.loadBearing: `every`: the declarations in the shape of every guarantee of the task. `lemmas`: each lemma (a theorem that is not a requirement) in any shape, with the number of guarantees whose shape contains it.
definitions.hole: A declaration whose type or value contains `sorryAx`, as the Lean kernel records it (an explicit `sorry`: `sorry`; one Lean inserted for an elaboration error: `error`), including a required theorem left `sorry`. Only declarations in some shape are seen this way; a `sorry` in a declaration of the candidate that no guarantee reaches is listed under build.sorryOutsideShapes, from Lean's `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings, and no guarantee hangs from it.
definitions.hangsFrom: The holes in a guarantee's shape, or the guarantee itself when it is a hole. A guarantee hangs from those holes.
definitions.complete: A guarantee with no hole in its shape, that is not a hole itself, in a candidate that builds without errors.

rule: Nodes are the declarations reached from the requirement theorems by following the constants each declaration's type and value use, as the Lean kernel sees them, restricted to the candidate (final.lean) and the locked specification. Compiler-generated declarations are walked through, so their uses count for the declaration that generated them; constructors, recursors and projections count as their type; Lean's core library and ProofForgeFin are not shown (the ProofForgeFin declarations a node mentions are listed under its `library`). A declaration of the candidate that no requirement uses is left out and listed under excluded. An edge [a, b] means a uses b.

lean.runner: local release build of the toolchain (PF_LEAN_HOME)

statement.text: a given-in swap between two tokens of the pool goes through, for any well-behaved math, when the scaling factor of the token out is positive and the fee is below 100%.

readme.text: for well-behaved math, a given-in swap between two tokens of the pool goes through when the token out has a positive scaling factor and the fee is below 100%

statement.text: a given-out swap between two tokens of the pool goes through, for any well-behaved math, when the exact amount out rounded up is below the pool's balance of that token (both in 18-decimal units), the scaling factor of the token in is positive and the fee is below 100%.

readme.text: for well-behaved math, a given-out swap goes through when the exact amount out rounded up is below the pool's scaled balance of that token, the token in has a positive scaling factor and the fee is below 100%

statement.text: in a given-in swap the trader receives at most what the math prices the exact amount in, net of the fee, rounded down: `y * rate_out / 1e18` is at most `outGivenIn` of that amount. Rounding never pays out more than the trader paid for.

readme.text: for monotone prices, the trader receives at most what the math prices the exact amount in, net of the fee, rounded down

statement.text: and it receives at least what the math prices one raw unit less than the net amount in, less one raw unit out: the rounding costs the trader at most one unit on each side.

readme.text: and at least what the math prices one raw unit less, less one raw unit out

statement.text: in a given-out swap the trader is charged, after the fee, at least what the math prices the exact amount out rounded up to a whole 18-decimal unit: `c * (1 - fee) * rate_in / 1e18` is at least `outPrice`. Rounding never lets the trader take more than it pays for.

readme.text: for monotone prices, the charge, after the fee, is at least what the math prices the exact amount out rounded up to a whole 18-decimal unit

statement.text: and one raw unit less than the charge, after the fee, is below that price plus one raw unit of the token in: the rounding costs the trader at most one unit for the conversion back to raw units and one for the fee.

readme.text: and one raw unit less than the charge is below that price plus one raw unit: at most one unit for the conversion back and one for the fee

statement.text: for any well-behaved math, a swap that goes through never lowers the pool's value as the pool measures it (`value`).

readme.text: for well-behaved math, a swap that goes through never lowers the pool's value

statement.text: for any well-behaved math, any pool and any batch of swaps of either kind, a batch that goes through never lowers the pool's value as the pool measures it. The rounding of one swap cannot be repeated inside a batch to drain the pool.

readme.text: for well-behaved math, any pool and any batch of swaps of either kind, a batch that goes through never lowers the pool's value
